description_full: ATN International, Inc., through its subsidiaries, provides digital infrastructure and communications services to residential, business, and government customers in the United States, Guyana, the US Virgin Islands, Bermuda, and internationally. It operates through International Telecom and US Telecom segments. The company offers fixed data and voice telecommunication services comprising fiber broadband and data solutions; carrier telecommunication services consisting of the leasing of tower and transport facilities, wholesale roaming and long-distance voice services, site maintenance, and international long-distance services; and mobile telecommunication services over wireless networks, including voice, messaging, and data services. It also provides information technology managed services, such as network, application, infrastructure, and hosting services; and repairs and sells handsets and other accessories. ATN International, Inc. was formerly known as Atlantic Tele-Network, Inc. and changed its name to ATN International, Inc. in June 2016. The company was founded in 1987 and is headquartered in Beverly, Massachusetts.

financial_summary: ATN International, Inc. is a small-cap communication services business with a $432M market cap on $728M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +0% over the past three years and +7% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 1% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
The business throws off $44M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -8.9% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.9× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 0.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 34% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
